title: [Mouse without Border] Easy Mouse's Ctrl/Shift keybind failing for Windows 10

status.label: Likely duplicate of Easy Mouse gating report
status.detail: Open issue #39710 tracks Easy Mouse moving between machines without the configured key.

judgment.rationale: The reporter confirms failure on 0.101.2362 and says identical settings work on Windows 11 but not Windows 10. Open issue #39710 describes Mouse Without Borders ignoring the configured shortcut and moving between machines without the selected key, matching the central behavior. The Win10/Win11 comparison is useful additional evidence for that tracker, not enough to establish a separate cause.
evidence: PowerToys 0.101.2362 Stable; Mouse Without Borders; Windows 10 22H2 paired with Windows 11 26H2.
The Windows 10 machine crosses without the selected Ctrl/Shift key and wakes the other machine; Windows 11 with identical settings works.
The latest user comment confirms testing 0.101.2362.
Open issue #39710 reports Easy Mouse moving between machines without its configured key and has no recorded fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Consolidate the Windows 10/11 comparison and wake-up consequence with open issue #39710.

fix_assessment.rationale: This likely duplicates the unresolved Easy Mouse gate issue in #39710; no separate code fix should be proposed until reports are consolidated or a distinct Windows 10 path is established.

issue_context.summary: Easy Mouse crosses from the Windows 10 machine without the configured Ctrl/Shift key even though the paired Windows 11 machine with identical settings behaves correctly.
known_information: Setup pairs Windows 10 22H2 and Windows 11 26H2; failure occurs on Windows 10.
The reporter expects the selected Ctrl/Shift gate to block crossing and says the other machine wakes.
The exact selected key and crossing direction are not specified.
Open issue #39710 reports Easy Mouse ignoring its selected shortcut and moving without the key.
inferences: The Win10/Win11 difference may be a platform-specific variation of #39710, but the report does not establish a distinct mechanism.
issue_context.analysis: An unresolved report already covers the same core behavior. Consolidating the new OS comparison and wake-up consequence avoids parallel issue/fix work while preserving the platform distinction.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and both comments; the author confirms testing 0.101.2362.
Read open #39710: it reports Easy Mouse ignoring shortcut gating and moving without the key; no fix is recorded.
The current report’s OS-specific contrast is retained as additional evidence; no distinct path is established.

comment.body: This appears to overlap the open Easy Mouse gating report in #39710, which also describes crossing between machines without the configured key. Please consolidate the additional evidence there: it reproduces on 0.101.2362, occurs on the Windows 10 22H2 machine while the paired Windows 11 26H2 machine works with identical settings, and can wake the other device. If maintainers find a distinct Windows 10 path, retain this issue separately.

upstream_safety.detail: No upstream or fork issue/PR writes were made.
